In the said application, it was specifically contended that sample  was collected by the complainant Food Inspector on 04.02.2006.

The HC-NIC Page 4 of 17 Created On Thu Feb 04 01:54:00 IST 2016 R/CR.RA/475/2011 JUDGMENT manufacturing  date of the said sample/biscuit was November 2005 and the said sample was best for  u s e b e f o r e s i x m o n t h s f r o m t h e d a t e o f p a c k i n g . T h u s , t h e  expiry date of the said sample was six months from the date of packing i.e. 6 months from  November 2005.
Hence, the expiry date of the sample was April, 2006.
Public analyst  submitted his report on 08.03.2006.
The competent authority gave his sanction on  12.07.2006 and thereafter the complainant filed the complaint on 22.08.2006 before the  learned Chief Judicial Magistrate.
Thus, it is an admitted position that the complaint was  filed by the Food Inspector after the expiry of the sample.

Hence, when the  complaint was filed before the concerned Magistrate Court, self life of the sample had  e x p i r e d . T h e r e s p o n d e n t s a c c u s e d t h e r e f o r e c o u l d n o t r e q u e s t t o t h e  Trial Court for sending the sample to the Central Food Laboratory and therefore, they had lost  the opportunity for sending the sample to the Central Food Laboratory.
Thus, prejudice is  caused to the respondentsaccused.

The complainant has thereby  violated the mandatory provision of Section 13(2) of the Act and therefore, the Trial Court  has rightly HC-NIC Page 5 of 17 Created On Thu Feb 04 01:54:00 IST 2016 R/CR.RA/475/2011 JUDGMENT discharged the accused.

I t i s a l s o c l e a r t h a t t h e  complaint had been filed on the 2nd July 2002 which is about a month short  o f t h e e x p i r y d a t e o f t h e d r u g a n d a s s u c h h a d t h e a c c u s e d  a p p e l l a n t a p p e a r e d b e f o r e t h e M a g i s t r a t e e v e n  on 2nd July 2002 it would have been well nigh impossible to get the sample  State Of Gujarat - Thro' S A Patel vs Nareshkumar Gordhandas Hotvani & on 1 February, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36485950/

This is begging the question.

We find that there is no explanation as to why  the complaint itself had been filed about a month before the expiry of  the shelf life of the drug and concededly the filing of the complaint had  nothing to do with the appearance of the accused in response to the HC-NIC Page 12 of 17 Created On Thu Feb 04 01:54:00 IST 2016 R/CR.RA/475/2011 JUDGMENT notices which were to be issued by the Court after the complaint  had been filed.

We  are, therefore, of the opinion that the facts of the case suggest that the  appellants have been deprived of a valuable right under  Section 25(3) and 25(4) of the Act which must necessitate the quashing of the  proceedings against them."
